source.quote: MHDT Labs' own page for the Orchid, read 2026-11-25. « Orchid DAC is a non over-sampling, no digital filter, structured DAC. » « Orchid DAC is capable of up to 24bits/192kHz digital signal inputs yet remains driving legendary TDA1541A R-2R digital to analog output. » « All inputs support 16/24 bits/ 32 kHz up to 192 kHz » « Total four independent digital inputs; BNC, USB, RCA and Toslink. » « Tube buffered output, tube in stalled is 5670 tube. » - the spacing is the page's. « Digital Receiver CS8416 » « D/A converter TDA1541A (standard version w/o suffix) ». No DSD figure anywhere. The family table gives « DAC Chip Construction: R/2R Multi Bits » and « Output Format: 16bits » for this model.

facts.chip: « D/A converter TDA1541A (standard version w/o suffix) » - the Philips multibit part, with « Digital Receiver CS8416 » in front of it and a « 5670 tube » buffering the output. The tube is the OUTPUT stage, not the converter.

device_settings.why: « a non over-sampling, no digital filter, structured DAC » - there is nothing to turn off. That is the precondition `correctable` requires, met by construction rather than by a menu, as on the LampizatOr Pacific 5. The maker says it of every model in the range, in those words, on every page.

_verification_des_conditions_tentee_et_n: mhdtlab.com links no terms, legal or copyright page from its navigation, and the fetched pages carry no copyright footer at all - it is an old-style hand-built site. The reader was careful to say that this is « no terms page found, so no prohibition could be checked. This is not a finding of 'no prohibition.' » The facts are recorded, because the rule is to integrate unless explicitly forbidden and nothing forbidding was found; the quality of the check is recorded with them, as it was for Burson and Mytek.
_NOS_ici_veut_dire_NON_SUR_ECHANTILLONNE: This is the maker vocabulary/nos-means-two-things.json was most afraid of: tube-output converters, where NOS valves and non-oversampling meet on one page. The reader checked every page read on both sites and reported: « No fetched page from either site contains 'NOS' or 'New Old Stock.' » MHDT writes « non over-sampling » IN FULL, every time, and names its valve by type. So the ambiguity the vocabulary note predicted does not arise here - not because it was resolved, but because this maker never uses the abbreviation.
_LE_PREMIER_APPAREIL_DE_LA_BASE_DONT_LE_: « a non over-sampling, no digital filter, structured DAC ». Nine makers in three days have stated a filter COUNT and withheld the names; this one says there is no filter at all. For an engine that is the most actionable sentence a page can carry: everything upstream arrives as it was sent, and `correctable` is true on the field's own definition rather than by elimination. Seven NOS devices are now recorded and this is the only family where it is the design rather than a setting.
_une_entree_BNC_qui_na_pas_de_cle: « Total four independent digital inputs; BNC, USB, RCA and Toslink. » BNC and RCA are both S/PDIF on different sockets - the distinction Naim, Wadax and Hegel have all raised - so three keys hold four inputs here, with no figure lost since « All inputs support 16/24 bits/ 32 kHz up to 192 kHz » covers them together.
_le_FORMAT_DE_SORTIE_est_16_bits_et_lent: The family table gives « Output Format: 16bits » for this model while every input accepts 24. The TDA1541A is a 16-bit part. So eight bits are discarded somewhere between the socket and the ladder, which is a property of the conversion and not of the input - `bits` is 24, what the device ACCEPTS, and the 16 lives in `chip`. Same shape as the Soekris ladder depth and the Schiit Yggdrasil's contested `bits`, and the third time in two days that a maker publishes both numbers and the schema can hold one.
